subject: bakery
title: Ingredients and Equipments
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Fill in the blanks and write the correct answers.

questions.q: The ________ portion of milk is called cream.
questions.answer: Fat (cream is the skimmed milk fat).

questions.q: ________ chambers are cabinets with temperature and humidity control.
questions.answer: Proving.

questions.q: A proving chamber, oven and table are all ________ equipment.
questions.answer: Heavy.

questions.q: The chemical name of ________ is sodium chloride.
questions.answer: Salt.

questions.q: Whole wheat flour consists of bran, ________ and germ.
questions.answer: Endosperm.

questions.q: ________ is obtained by milling of wheat.
questions.answer: Flour.

questions.q: Dry ________ is available in granular form.
questions.answer: Yeast.

questions.q: Yeast is a ________ raising agent.
questions.answer: Biological (it is a living micro-organism that produces carbon dioxide).

questions.q: In ________ flour the coarser part of the bran is removed.
questions.answer: Brown.

questions.q: A fresh egg ________ in water while a stale egg floats.
questions.answer: Sinks.

questions.q: Brown flour is used for making ________.
questions.answer: Brown bread.

questions.q: Milk contains about ________ per cent water.

sections.title: State whether the following statements are True or False.

questions.q: Fresh yeast may be stored at room temperature.
questions.answer: False. Fresh yeast is kept in a refrigerator (a couple of weeks) or frozen.

questions.q: Salt controls yeast activity.
questions.answer: True. It controls the speed of fermentation in yeast aerated goods.

questions.q: A fresh egg sinks in water.
questions.answer: True. A stale egg floats.

questions.q: Salt contains 40% chlorine and 60% sodium.
questions.answer: False. It contains 40% sodium and 60% chlorine.

questions.q: Margarine is a type of fat.
questions.answer: True. It is a shortening agent made from hydrogenated oils.

questions.q: A rolling pin is an electric tool.
questions.answer: False. It is a hand tool (light equipment).

questions.q: Only steel preparation tables are found in a bakery.
questions.answer: False. The table tops may also be made of marble.

questions.q: Brown sugar is refined sugar.
questions.answer: False. Brown sugars are unrefined raw sugars.

questions.q: Corn flour thickens custards.
questions.answer: True. It is used as a thickening agent.

questions.q: Milk contains about 87% of water.
questions.answer: True.

questions.q: A 'turn table' is a heavy equipment.
questions.answer: False. It is light equipment.

questions.q: The temperature of an electric oven cannot be controlled.
questions.answer: False. An electric oven has a thermostat which makes temperature regulation easier.

questions.q: One high pressure gas burner is a must for a bakery unit.
questions.answer: False. One low pressure gas burner is a must.

questions.q: Butter contains about 85% fat.
questions.answer: True.

questions.q: Yeast is available in dry form only.
questions.answer: False. It is available both fresh and dry.

questions.q: Whole wheat flour is 'atta' in Hindi.
questions.answer: True.

questions.q: 'Caster sugar' is a finer form of grain sugar.
questions.answer: True.

questions.q: A peeler is used to peel potatoes only.
questions.answer: False. It is used to peel vegetables and fruits in general.

questions.q: Milk is 100% water.
questions.answer: False. It contains about 87% water.

questions.q: Dry yeast is used in half the quantity of fresh yeast.
questions.answer: True. It is more concentrated.

questions.q: Proving chambers have time control only.
questions.answer: False. They have temperature and humidity control.

questions.q: The only type of sugar used in a bakery is grain sugar.
questions.answer: False. Castor, icing, brown sugar, golden syrup, treacle, honey, glucose and others are also used.

questions.q: Self raising flour has higher protein content and is used for making bread.
questions.answer: False. Strong flour has higher protein and is used for bread; self raising flour has the raising agent mixed in.

sections.title: Answer the following questions (five points each).

questions.q: Mention any 5 small / light equipment with their uses.
questions.answer: (i) Palette knife: to spread icing and lift biscuits. (ii) Sieve: to sift flour and remove lumps. (iii) Rolling pin: to roll out dough and pastes. (iv) Whisk: to beat eggs and cream. (v) Piping bag with nozzle: to pipe icing and make designs.

questions.q: Differentiate between dry and fresh yeast.
questions.answer: (i) Fresh yeast is available from bakers and speciality stores; dry yeast from provision stores. (ii) Fresh yeast is sold in 1/2 kg packs wrapped in butter paper; dry yeast in small sachets. (iii) Fresh yeast is pale beige, firm but crumbly with a fruity smell; dry yeast is in granules and a little darker. (iv) Fresh yeast is stored in a refrigerator for a couple of weeks (frozen for months); sealed dry yeast keeps for months in a cool cupboard but should be used within a month of opening. (v) Fresh yeast gives better products; dry yeast is used in half the quantity because it is more concentrated.

questions.q: Mention any 5 sweeteners used in bakery with their uses.
questions.answer: (i) Grain sugar: general sweetening. (ii) Castor sugar: finer, for creaming in cakes. (iii) Icing sugar: very fine powder for icing, glazes, dusting and almond paste. (iv) Brown sugar: gives colour and flavour to rich cakes. (v) Golden syrup / treacle / honey / liquid glucose: for ginger cakes and biscuits, dark fruit cakes, gingerbreads and sugar boiling.

questions.q: List any five baking ingredients and mention their uses.
questions.answer: (i) Flour: forms the bulk and structure of bakery products. (ii) Yeast: ferments sugar and produces carbon dioxide that raises the dough. (iii) Baking powder: chemical raising agent. (iv) Salt: gives flavour, controls the speed of fermentation and strengthens gluten. (v) Eggs: form the structure and give colour; the yolk emulsifies and is used as a glaze.

questions.q: Classify the ingredients used in a bakery according to their keeping quality, with examples.
questions.answer: (i) Non-perishable: kept for more than a month at room temperature, e.g. flour, sugar, salt, spices. (ii) Perishable: can be stored for a couple of days at the most at proper temperature, e.g. milk, cream, fresh fruits and vegetables, meat. (iii) Semi-perishable: need proper storage temperature but keep longer than perishables, e.g. butter and other fats, chocolates, eggs, opened tins.
